title: Human-readable slug for containers, set at creation and usable in template interpolation
description:
Give breakable containers a stable, human-readable slug set at creation, and expose it to template interpolation so plan-doc paths and grouping labels read as `dev/active/user-auth-plan.md` instead of an opaque hash.

## Background

The `plan` template's planning node interpolates the container's identifier into its plan-doc path (`.jit/templates.toml`). Today that path uses the container's 8-char `short_id`, e.g. `dev/active/2821e177-plan.md`. The short ID is a non-descriptive hash: a reader browsing `dev/active/` cannot tell what an epic is about, and the same opacity affects any other template token that surfaces the container to humans.

The content standards already establish this preference for grouping labels: strategic labels use a kebab-case slug describing the bucket (`epic:user-auth`), never the short ID, because slugs are stable across renames, navigable, and meaningful when grepped. Extending a first-class slug to the issue model lets plan-doc filenames and other interpolated surfaces inherit the same readability, and removes the current dependency on the hash being unique enough for a filename.

`InterpolationContext` (`crates/jit/src/commands/template.rs`) resolves `{container.id}`, `{container.short_id}`, `{container.title}`, `{container.hard_criteria}`. A slug adds one more resolvable token.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] [hard] REQ-1: An issue can carry a slug — a stable, human-readable identifier distinct from its UUID and `short_id`. The slug is validated as lowercase kebab-case and non-empty; an invalid slug is rejected at write time.
- [ ] [hard] REQ-2: Creating a breakable container (a type appearing in some template's `applies_to`) guarantees the created issue has a slug present, so no breakable container can exist without one.
- [ ] [hard] REQ-3: Template interpolation resolves a `{container.slug}` token, so a node `doc` template of `dev/active/{container.slug}-plan.md` produces a slug-based path at apply time.
- [ ] [hard] REQ-4: Two distinct live containers cannot resolve to the same slug-derived plan-doc path (slug collisions that would clobber a plan doc are prevented or disambiguated).

## Notes

- The plan-doc template was already switched from `{container.id}` to `{container.short_id}` as an interim readability step; this issue supersedes that by offering a descriptive `{container.slug}`.
- Owner-owned design forks to settle during planning, not pre-decided here:
  - **Provenance** — require the creator to supply the slug vs. derive it deterministically from the title with an override.
  - **Uniqueness scope** — enforce global uniqueness, uniqueness among live (non-archived) containers, or only disambiguate on filename collision.
  - **Applicability** — slug on breakable containers only vs. every issue.
